column1: # expected.tsv --- the oracle. Per oracle-transfers, the reusable asset is the fixtures and their
# expected counts, NOT gauge.sh: rewrite the tool in any language and it must still produce these
# Two kinds of check ride on this file and they catch different things:
#   COUNTS       exact num/den/ratio per doc per gauge -- catches a regression in any pattern.
#   ORDERING     jacket >= middling >= rebuilt on every gauge -- catches a change that keeps the
#                numbers stable-looking but destroys the gauge's power to discriminate. A gauge
#                whose ordering collapses is decoration, even if its counts still "pass".
# The three fixtures are deliberately spread: jacket affords nothing (every denominator 0, so
# every ratio is INF), rebuilt affords plenty, and middling exists so the DIVISION path and the
# numeric DELTA path are actually exercised -- with only the two extremes, ratio() never divides.
